description: JVM function values and wrappers slice (ISSUE-0098), migrated to the v1.2 module shape. JVM-only fixtures run the real DEAL frontend (lexer → parser → name resolver → type checker) → real JvmBackend codegen → javac subprocess → java subprocess executing the emitted artifact (the harness fails a fixture whose codegen or JVM execution is bypassed). Covered forms: first-class function values in typed and inferred variables, indirect calls through variables/parameters/module fields and call-result callees, callbacks with primitive/string/null signatures, returning function values, the int/number conversion intrinsics as function values (exact and arity-extended), arity-extension adapters at variable-initializer and assignment positions — module functions and intrinsics delegate through the module-class-QUALIFIED static call, and never-reassigned locals/parameters snapshot (reassigned bindings and non-identifier adapter values are E6000 until ISSUE-0110, pinned in JvmBackendTest) — E8010 runtime signature checks at callback and return boundaries with the checked value expression evaluated FIRST (evaluate-then-check side-effect order pinned cross-backend), wrapper reference equality, recursion routed through the wrapper, wrapper-name collisions (a function named invoke or descriptor delegates through the qualified static member — never a recursion into the wrapper's own invoke or a javac failure on the descriptor field), and six frontend compile-error gates (E3001 parameter/return signature mismatch, E5004 reverse arity, E3009/E5001 indirect-call arity/argument mismatch, E3008 non-function callee) rejected before any backend. Ten fixtures run under both backends as cross-backend parity with real luajit. Four multi-module fixtures pin the cross-module function-value flow through the SHARED $DealRt wrapper carriers (ISSUE-0301): the callback-in shape, the arity-extension argument/E8010 boundary, the return-out shape, and the call-result callee all execute through the real pipeline — one shared wrapper class per signature, so wrapper values cross module boundaries with reference identity and the complete canonical descriptor (the pre-fix per-module wrapper classes were artifacts javac rejected after the CLI reported success). Each entry module exports non-async main(): null per the v1.2 selected-entry rule. The v1.1 module-level/load-time shapes — module-field load-time indirect calls and reassignment, the live field-adapter reassignment parity pair, and the four LuaJIT load-time reference pins (load-time-called function-body assignment/indirect-call, module-level call-result callees) — are v1.2 grammar gates (E1049): the v1.2 module top level holds only declarations, so those shapes are rejected before any backend. Two LuaJIT-only fixtures pin the reference semantics of the in-function shapes the JVM slice conservatively rejects with E6000 (the reassigned-local and side-effecting call-result adapters — the call-result pin now re-evaluates picker() per invoke with console markers, since the v1.2 grammar removed the v1.1 module-field counter).

tests.name: jvm-fv-typed-variable-indirect-call
tests.description: First-class function value: a function declaration assigned to a typed variable of its exact signature and called indirectly through the variable (f(20, 22) = 42) — the call dispatches through the emitted wrapper's invoke, not a direct static call

tests.name: jvm-fv-inferred-variable
tests.description: Type inference for function values: `let f = dbl` infers the function type without an annotation and calls through the inferred wrapper (dbl(21) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-callback-param
tests.description: Callback through a function-typed parameter: apply(f: (int)=>int, v) calls its parameter indirectly (apply(inc, 41) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-callback-mixed-signatures
tests.description: Callback with a boolean/string signature: choose(f, true) calls the stored three-parameter function with boolean and string arguments and returns "jvm"

tests.name: jvm-fv-return-function-value
tests.description: Returning a function value: picker() returns the wrapped inc and the result is invoked immediately (picker()(41) = 42) — the callee is a call expression, dispatched through the returned wrapper

tests.name: jvm-fv-null-signatures
tests.description: Null in function signatures: () => null and (null) => int function values are stored, the void wrapper is invoked as a statement, and the null-parameter wrapper is called with null (wn(null) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-function-equality
tests.description: Function-value equality is wrapper reference identity: two reads of the same declaration's wrapper field compare equal (f === g with both holding inc), matching LuaJIT's wrapper-table identity

tests.name: jvm-fv-callback-chain
tests.description: A function value passed through a two-level callback chain: twice(inc, 20) applies the stored wrapper twice (20 + 1 + 1 = 22)

tests.name: jvm-fv-intrinsic-value-error
tests.description: A runtime error propagates through the intrinsic function-value wrapper: int(41.5) through the stored wrapper raises E8001 (non-integer number), exactly like the direct intrinsic call

tests.name: jvm-fv-sig-check-callback-error
tests.description: Signature check at a callback parameter boundary: passing (int)=>int where (int,string)=>int is declared compiles (arity extension) but raises E8010 at the parameter boundary when apply is entered, exactly like LuaJIT's wrapper check

tests.name: jvm-fv-sig-check-return-error
tests.description: Signature check at a return boundary: returning (int)=>int from a function declared (int,int)=>int compiles (arity extension) but raises E8010 when picker's return value crosses the declared boundary, exactly like LuaJIT's return check

tests.name: jvm-fv-frontend-sig-return-type
tests.description: Signature failure (return type): () => string is not assignable to an () => int variable — E3001 before any backend runs

tests.name: jvm-fv-frontend-indirect-arity
tests.description: Indirect-call arity failure: calling a one-parameter function value with two arguments is E3009 before any backend runs

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-callback-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): the callback apply(inc, 41) = 42 shape runs through both backends' real codegen and execution and prints the same marker

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-arity-assign-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): the arity-extension assignment adapter ignores the extra parameter on both backends (f(41, 999) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-intrinsic-value-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): the int intrinsic stored as a function value converts through the wrapper on both backends (ci(42.0) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-reassignment-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): reassigning a function-typed variable retargets later calls on both backends (f = dbl; f(21) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-boolean-boundary-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): an indirect call through an inferred function-typed variable applies the same typed boolean boundary as a direct call — a past-end boolean[] read's nil passed through && as the boolean argument fails the parameter boundary with E8001, exit 1 on both backends (the JVM converts the boxed temporary with booleanNotNull at the argument position: E8001 "expected boolean, got null"; LuaJIT's check_boolean(nil) at callee entry).

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-e8010-callback-eval-order
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): at an E8010 callback-parameter check position the argument value expressions are evaluated before the check raises — the checked argument's value expression prints its pre marker and the later argument's value prints its post marker, in that order, before the E8010 (spec §Operational semantics rule 2), and the E8010 still follows on both backends (exit 1). The v1.2 grammar removed the v1.1 module-field counter, so the order is pinned with console markers

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-e8010-return-eval
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): at an E8010 return-boundary check position the returned value expression is evaluated before the check raises — markF logs its marker and only then does the E8010 fire on both backends (exit 1); the pre-fix JVM dropped the side effect entirely

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-e8010-two-mismatched-args
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): one call with TWO arity-mismatched function-valued arguments whose later value expression is impure (pickZero logs before returning) — both value expressions evaluate left to right (the marker prints) and only then does the FIRST parameter's boundary check raise E8010 with the first parameter's descriptor (the message carries 'got (int)->int'); the second parameter's descriptor ('got ()->int') is pinned never to print, and the emitted artifact must be valid Java — the pre-fix JVM materialized the later operand's raising construction into an ACTUAL-shape temporary ('Fn0_R_I __t0 = new Fn2_IS_R_I() {…}'), which the harness's javac step rejects ('incompatible types') and which would have raised the second parameter's check before the first's

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-callee-eval-order-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): a call-result callee evaluates COMPLETELY before any argument (spec §Operational semantics rule 1) even when a later argument hoists side-effecting pre-statements — picker() runs first and its past-end int[] read raises E8001 before bump()'s negative-index E8002 or the && operand's hoisted read can run, exit 1 on both backends (the pre-fix JVM hoisted bump()'s read first and raised E8002; 'negative array index' is pinned never to appear)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-callee-e8010-order-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): a call-result callee whose return boundary raises E8010 (picker returns (int)=>int where (int,boolean)=>int is declared) evaluates and raises BEFORE any argument — the hoisted bump() negative-index read and the && operand never run, so only E8010 appears and 'negative array index' never prints, exit 1 on both backends (the pre-fix JVM hoisted bump()'s read first and raised E8002)

tests.name: jvm-fv-lua-ref-reassigned-adapter
tests.description: LuaJIT reference semantics for the reassigned-local adapter shape that the JVM slice conservatively rejects with E6000 (pinned in JvmBackendTest.testFunctionValues): LuaJIT's adapter reads the binding live on every invoke, so f = dbl retargets the earlier adapter (h(10, 999) = 20)

tests.name: jvm-fv-lua-ref-callresult-adapter
tests.description: LuaJIT reference semantics for the side-effecting call-result adapter shape that the JVM slice conservatively rejects with E6000 (pinned in JvmBackendTest.testFunctionValues): LuaJIT's adapter re-evaluates picker() on EVERY invoke — two invokes run picker twice, printing the marker twice — and the two invokes compute 33 + 33 = 66; a creation-time-only evaluation would print the marker once (the v1.2 grammar removed the v1.1 module-field counter, so the re-evaluation is pinned with console markers)

tests.name: jvm-fv-xmod-callback-arg
tests.description: Cross-module callback on the shared $DealRt carrier: a callback passed INTO an imported project module's function-typed parameter — Main's inc wrapper and Lib's apply parameter hold the SAME shared $DealRt wrapper class, so Lib.apply(inc, 41) computes 42 across the module boundary (the pre-fix per-module wrapper classes made the artifact javac-rejected after the CLI reported success). The v1.2 selected-entry rule is satisfied by the exported non-async main(): null.

modules.lib.deal: export function apply(f: (x: int) => int, v: int): int { return f(v); }

tests.name: jvm-fv-xmod-arity-extension-arg-e8010
tests.description: Cross-module E8010 boundary on the shared $DealRt carrier: (x:int)=>int passed to an imported (a:int,b:string)=>int parameter compiles (arity extension) and raises E8010 "function signature mismatch: expected (int,string)->int, got (int)->int" at the imported call's parameter boundary — the same check the same-module path emits, now applied to the imported member call's declared parameter targets. The v1.2 selected-entry rule is satisfied by the exported non-async main(): null.

modules.lib.deal: export function apply2(f: (a: int, b: string) => int, v: int): int { return f(v, "i"); }

tests.name: jvm-fv-xmod-return-out
tests.description: Cross-module function-value return on the shared $DealRt carrier: lib.picker() returns its inc wrapper, the caller stores it in a typed (x:int)=>int variable, and f(41) computes 42 — one shared wrapper class, no conversion adapter, reference identity preserved across the module boundary (the pre-fix emission 'Fn1_I_R_I f = Lib.picker();' was javac-rejected). The v1.2 selected-entry rule is satisfied by the exported non-async main(): null.

modules.lib.deal:
export function picker(): (x: int) => int { return inc; }
function inc(x: int): int { return x + 1; }

tests.name: jvm-fv-xmod-callresult-callee
tests.description: Cross-module call-result callee on the shared $DealRt carrier: lib.picker()(41) materializes the imported call result into a caller-typed temporary of the SAME shared wrapper class and invokes it — 42 (the pre-fix emission typed the temporary with the caller module's per-module wrapper class against the defining module's return type and javac rejected the artifact). The v1.2 selected-entry rule is satisfied by the exported non-async main(): null.

modules.lib.deal:
export function picker(): (x: int) => int { return inc; }
function inc(x: int): int { return x + 1; }

tests.name: jvm-fv-invoke-name-collision
tests.description: Review 0009 (MR-0081): a DEAL function named `invoke` — the emitted wrapper classes' dispatch method name — works as a direct value, an arity-adapted value, and a callback without recursion or javac failure: the declaration wrapper and the arity adapter delegate to the module-class-QUALIFIED static method (Main.invoke(p0)), never to a bare `invoke` that would resolve to the anonymous wrapper's own invoke (f(41) + g(0, 999) + apply(invoke, 0) = 42 + 1 + 1 = 44)

tests.name: jvm-fv-descriptor-name-collision
tests.description: Review 0009 companion: a DEAL function named `descriptor` — the emitted wrapper classes' descriptor field name — works as an arity-adapted value without a javac failure: the adapter's delegation is module-class-qualified, so the bare name never resolves to the wrapper shape class's descriptor field (f(21, 999) = 42)
